outcome: A cast spell moves from its zone to the stack and its costs are paid; an illegal cast is reverted to the prior game state.
The spell moves to the top of the stack with the caster as controller and modified characteristics applied.
A spell cannot choose the same object twice for one instance of the word target, and its targets must be legal and obey must-target effects.
A proposed spell that is illegal is not cast and the game returns to the state before it was proposed.
The total cost is the base cost plus increases minus reductions, never below zero mana, and is locked in.
The locked-in total cost is paid in full, with the costs' zone changes and mana spent, and partial payment is not allowed.
Abilities that trigger on a spell being cast or put onto the stack fire once the spell is cast.
A player may begin casting a spell only if some rule or effect allows it and none prohibits it.
A prohibition that could be avoided by a choice made during proposal does not stop the player from beginning to cast.
Cast-as-though-flash permission applies if a choice made during proposal could trigger it.
A cast-as-though-flash permission conditional on an alternative or additional cost lets the player begin casting.
A spell with flash only when conditions hold can be begun at instant speed when they hold.
Alternative characteristics replace the object's characteristics when determining whether it is legal to cast.
A face-down exiled card can be cast only if its controller can look at it.
If the player is no longer allowed to cast after proposal the cast is reverted, but later changes during cost payment or after casting do not undo it.
A spell begun with flash by a condition can finish being cast after the condition stops holding.
A cost-altering spell on the stack does not change the cost of spells already on the stack.
